properties.project_name: Building 12 Plaza and Market Square -- approximate
properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4114008 and 4114004 (recorded 2019-02-07, 2020-10-23; mapped 2019-03-14, 2021-07-07; active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass); REDONE 2026-09-17 (first pass) after a user-reported visual bug (this plaza appeared to render as a thin diagonal ribbon crossing Maryland St into the E2/H1 area, nowhere near Building 12) -- traced from the diagram's own green pixel fill, clipped tightly against Building 2/D/12, producing a conservative ~0.35-acre result. REDONE AGAIN 2026-09-17 (second pass, same day) after the user pointed out this was still wrong: the D4D drawing shows Buildings 2, D, and 12 coming together with green space to fill the ENTIRE street block (Louisiana St to Maryland St), but the diagram-pixel-clip approach left large unaccounted gaps (~17-18m strips of bare pavement between Building 2/12's real satellite-verified positions and the diagram's own, less precisely-drawn green boundary) that didn't match either the drawing's intent or satellite reality. Switched approach entirely: used this project's own src/block_fit.py (load_blocks() + find_containing_block()) to get the REAL, street-polygonized city block bounded by Louisiana St and Maryland St (the same tool used to place Elevation Sky Park and Building 21's earlier approximations), unioned it with Parcel D's own geometry (D's north edge extends slightly beyond the polygonized block, toward the not-yet-built 21st St (NEW)), then subtracted Building 2's real/satellite-corrected geometry, Parcel D's own geometry, and Building 12's real Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) via shapely difference(). This directly guarantees the block reads as fully filled -- buildings plus this plaza, no gaps -- rather than depending on how precisely the diagram's own green pixels were drawn relative to each building. Verified via a rendered satellite overlay (with an explicit PathPatch, not a naive geopandas .plot(), to confirm the resulting hole around Building 12 is real and not a plotting artifact) that the result correctly excludes both buildings and covers the rest of the block. Resulting area ~5,590 sq m (~1.38 acres), much closer to the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres than either prior attempt. Confirmed zero overlap with C1, C2, HDY1/2, E1, and PKS. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: 'Building 12's real Assessor parcel is blklot 4114010' is our own lookup, not a D4D statement: DataSF's Assessor layer lists 4114010 as an active P70-MU lot at 1070 Maryland St (added 2020-10-23), the address other sources in this repo give for Building 12's tenants; DataSF does not name the lot 'Building 12'. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, regulatory_context, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- derived from a real, street-polygonized city block (not a diagram pixel-trace), subtracting Building 2, Parcel D, and Building 12's own committed geometries. This is a deliberate departure from pure diagram-tracing: since Figure 6.4.2's own green fill didn't precisely reach the real (satellite-corrected) edges of Building 2 and Building 12, using the real block boundary instead better matches both the drawing's evident intent (this block reads as fully built-out, buildings plus plaza, no gaps) and the satellite ground truth. The block polygon's north edge stops slightly short of Parcel D's own north edge (~14m, since the not-yet-built '21st St (NEW)' isn't in real street data) -- unioned with D's own extent to avoid an artificial gap there. Area (~1.38 acres) is close to, but still a bit under, the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres for this named space -- the cause of the gap is not established: the D4D (Section 3.9) also counts a Maryland Street Platform along Maryland St as part of the space and places the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, so the plaza's extent here may differ from the D4D's in more than one way (the dashed '15' box on the diagram is the legend's approximate location of the mid-block passage beside Building 15, not a boundary of this space).'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Open space with no Assessor lot of its own identified: DataSF's Assessor layer (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that the site is unaddressed and not subdivided is withdrawn; whether the plaza's block has its own lot has not been checked against the recorded final map.'; regulatory_context: 'Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.9), approximately 1.5 acres. Per Section 3.9, Market Square lies north of Building 12 (between Building 2 and Parcel D, entered from 21st St), the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, and the Maryland Street Platform along Building 12's Maryland St side; the file's block spans Louisiana St to Maryland St.'; notes: 'Newly added 2026-09-16 as part of a systematic pass adding this site's previously-untracked open space; geometry REDONE TWICE 2026-09-17 after user-caught issues -- see digitization_method. Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026): the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development.'. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner asked for the planned blocks that have Assessor lots under them to use those lots. DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004 (3,408 m2, active, recorded 2019-02-07, 2020-10-23), 52% of our earlier trace lies inside it and the trace covers 86% of it; against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off. The outline is now their union using the lots' own vertices (no simplification), in place of the traced shape of 5,580 m2. The lots were chosen by the owner; they leave out part of the open ground the earlier outline covered. geometry_type is now 'real' because the edges are recorded lot lines. The earlier sign-off covered the traced shape; this replacement was made at the owner's direction.
properties.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lot choice was made by the owner on a reading of the diagram and the satellite imagery; no document read ties these lots to the plaza. The lots do not cover all of the open ground the D4D draws around Buildings 2 and 12, so the earlier outline's extent is not reproduced. A building may sit back from the lot lines. The plaza is planned (Port Item 11A, memo dated Aug 7, 2026: the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004 (active), chosen by the owner as the lots under the plaza; no document names them as the plaza.
properties.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.9), approximately 1.5 acres. Per Section 3.9, Market Square lies north of Building 12 (between Building 2 and Parcel D, entered from 21st St), the Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd St, and the Maryland Street Platform along Building 12's Maryland St side; the mapped block spans Louisiana St to Maryland St.
properties.notes: The Building 12 Plaza of the Pier 70 Design for Development, shown as the union of Assessor lots 4114008 and 4114004 (see the accuracy note). Added 2026-09-16 together with this site's other previously untracked open space; geometry REDONE TWICE 2026-09-17 after problems with the shape were found. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Status 'planned' as of Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026): the balance of Phase 1, largely the Phase 1 parks and open space, will be built on a schedule that coincides with adjacent vertical development.
